rationale: Re-select the same region (ResNetEmbeddings + all four ResNetBasicLayer groups) and repair the previous trial's concrete numerical failure. Measured facts: clean median latency_ms is 4.225017 (project.json original_baseline) while the 88 CUDA kernels of one forward sum to 4152.3 us (call-resources.json, root call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 rank 0), so the window is GPU-bound with ~73 us of host headroom; the python_runtime collector corroborates (its cProfile window is dominated by torch._C._cuda_synchronize self 1.646 ms, with all nn.Module _call_impl/_wrapped_call_impl/__getattr__ wrapper cost ~0.43 ms under perturbation and overlapped in clean runs), so host-side plays (CUDA graphs, Python trimming) stay rejected - the binding contract additionally notes CUDA Graph replay does not rerun the Python hooks that quality coverage counts. Kernel composition of the 4152.3 us: conv math ~3045.6 us (73.3%, frozen: FP32, TF32 off, cudnn.benchmark off; ampere scudnn/winograd variants already selected), eager pointwise 889.7 us (21.4%: 20x cudnn::bn_fw_inf_1C11_kernel_NCHW = 425.4 us; 25x vectorized_elementwise covering 17 relu clamps + 8 CUDAFunctor residual adds = 464.3 us), max_pool_forward_nchw 198.2 us. The transformers 5.16.1 structure inside this region (modeling_resnet.py:65-69,85-93,113-136) runs each conv into a separate BN pass, a separate ReLU pass, and per block a separate residual add plus second ReLU - up to 5 full-tensor memory-bound passes per block for what is one elementwise expression y = relu(bn_affine(conv2(conv1(x))) + shortcut(x)); collapsing these to one pass per chain attacks exactly the 889.7 us pool. The edits are interdependent (block conv2's BN must fuse with the block-level add+ReLU; the stem BN with the stem ReLU), so this is one coherent region, not independent group edits; the 9 module boundaries give the replacement ownership of the fused chains while convs, the stem max-pool and the 3 shortcut conv+BN modules keep their observed parent dispatch. Concrete failure repaired (previous-feedback.txt + previous-candidate/candidate.py, not a re-explanation of a category): the trial ran and dispatch worked (run passed, all 9 required call sites invoked 2x, binding 'direct', coverage complete) but quality failed with 32000/32000 mismatches and max_abs_error 40.84. Root cause 1, causal from the code: the Triton kernels index a contiguous NCHW tensor as channel-major, base = c*hw with hw = N*H*W, so element offset c*(N*H*W)+linear lands in true channel (c*N + n) mod C - the per-channel BN affine constants a,b were applied to scrambled channels, and the route telemetry shows all 8 blocks executed 'triton_fused_bn_add_relu' with no fallback, so the corrupted output reached the logits; this is an indexing bug, not inherent fusion error, and the fix is to tile over [N*C, H*W] planes with true channel = plane % C (or decompose n,c explicitly). Root cause 2: the stem guard compared the 3-channel input against the 64-channel BN constants (int(x.shape[1]) != channels), so the stem always raised _Fallback (diagnostic event candidate.py:147, count 2) and silently ran the parent - the guard must compare input channels to num_channels and conv output channels to the BN size, otherwise the stem fusion is forfeited. Both bugs are in the rejected candidate only; the region boundary, parent/module dispatch and coverage model are proven viable by the same failed run. Alternatives rejected on measured evidence: cudnn.benchmark/TF32 (frozen numerical policy), channels_last (frozen NCHW batch semantics), host-side or graph capture (GPU-bound window + coverage semantics). Communication analysis is not applicable (single device, resources.json).
hypothesis: Replace the forward of ResNetEmbeddings and the 8 ResNetBasicLayer modules (region groups as in the previous trial, same current-discovery IDs) with corrected fused pointwise chains: conv1/conv2/stem conv stay on the observed parent Conv2d dispatch (cudnn kernels, bit-identical outputs); each chain then runs one Triton kernel - y = max(fma(x, a_c, b_c), 0) and y = max(fma(z, a_c, b_c) + s, 0) with a = weight*rsqrt(var+eps), b = bias - mean*a packed once at installation - with NCHW-correct indexing: grid over [N*C, H*W] planes, per-plane channel index pid % C addressing A/B, replacing the previous channel-major base = c*(N*H*W) scrambling that caused the 40.8 max_abs_error quality failure; the stem eligibility guard is fixed to check the 3-channel input against num_channels and the 64-channel conv output against the BN size so the stem actually fuses instead of falling back. Expected effect on the objective: the 42 eager pointwise launches (20 BN + 17 ReLU + 8 add, 889.7 us at ~0.9-1.4 TB/s effective) collapse to 17 single-pass kernels, cutting full-tensor traffic from 11 passes/block to 5 and 2 to 1 in the stem, so the pointwise pool should shrink to ~380-450 us and latency_ms from 4.225 to ~3.75-3.90 ms (-8 to -12%); the now-unblocked stem BN+ReLU fusion adds a small extra beyond the previous (never-measured, fallback-only) stem contribution. Numerics: conv outputs unchanged; the fused affine uses the same eval-BN formula with FMA-order differences of ~1 ULP per element, far below atol/rtol 1e-4, but this remains a hypothesis the framework's paired logits check and require_exact_top1 must confirm on the GPU - the previous trial's 40.8 error was the indexing bug and says nothing about the true fused drift. Unknowns to test rather than assume: top-2 logit gap sensitivity of the 3 fixture images under the drift; whether Triton JIT compilation lands fully in quality/warmup execution outside the 5 timed samples; whether packed derived constants (checkpoint parameters never mutated) are accepted under the frozen no-weight-change invariant; and whether the memory goal is preserved (fused outputs replace equal-sized intermediates, ~19 KB of packed constants added). Only the measured median latency_ms credits the gain.
